hero.title: OpinionMiner
hero.subtitle: A multilingual sentiment analysis engine designed for noisy, code-switched text and real-world opinion streams.

origin.pullQuote: Sentiment systems fail quietly when language is mixed and context is local.
paragraphs: OpinionMiner was built to process sentiment in conversational environments where users blend languages, slang, and domain-specific shorthand that traditional pipelines misclassify.
The project focuses on robust preprocessing, token normalization, and sentiment scoring strategies that preserve meaning in code-switched text rather than forcing monolingual assumptions.

architecture.title: Multilingual Text Normalization and Scoring Pipeline
architecture.description: A staged NLP pipeline for cleaning, language-aware token handling, and weighted sentiment inference.
architecture.narrative: The architecture decomposes sentiment analysis into normalization, feature extraction, and scoring phases so each stage can be tested and iterated independently. Language-aware preprocessing mitigates token drift, while weighted scoring supports interpretable outputs suitable for downstream dashboards or moderation workflows.

hardParts.title: Handling Sarcasm and Context Polarity Flips
hardParts.description: The most difficult engineering issue was sentiment inversion in context-heavy or sarcastic expressions.
hardParts.narrative: Literal token polarity performed poorly on sarcastic and context-dependent phrases, especially in mixed-language statements. The remediation introduced contextual heuristics, negation-aware transformations, and confidence-aware fallback logic to reduce brittle polarity assignments in ambiguous text.
